title: Minimax M2: Building the #1 Open Model – Olive Song, MiniMax
talk_summary: MiniMax's Olive Song presents M2, a 10B-active-parameter open-weight model tuned for coding and agentic tasks, and describes four training choices: scaled verifiable environments plus expert-developer reward models, interleaved thinking with tool calls, data perturbation pipelines for scaffold generalization, and small size enabling multi-agent parallelism.

takeaways.technique: Interleaved think-act loops instead of single tool-call rounds
takeaways.what_they_do: The model re-thinks after each tool response and decides whether the returned information is sufficient, repeating for many turns within one user request rather than doing one call-then-answer pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of just stopping um after one round of tool calling, it actually thinks again and reacts to the uh reacts to the environments to see if the information is enough
takeaways.numbers: tens to 100 tool-calling turns within one user interaction

takeaways.technique: Expert developers as reward/eval models for real deliverables
takeaways.what_they_do: In-house senior developers define problems, judge model behavior and final deliverables, and encode what is reliable and trustworthy as precise reward and evaluation signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually scale something called expert developers um as reward models

takeaways.technique: Small active-parameter model for parallel agent fan-out
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue a 10B-active model is cheap enough to run many copies in parallel for long agentic and research tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: because it is so small um and so cost effective it can really um support those long run agentic tasks and tasks that maybe um require some kind of parallelism

takeaways.technique: Perturbation across the whole operational space for scaffold robustness
takeaways.what_they_do: They vary system prompts, user prompts, chat template, tool schemas and tool responses in training data so the model adapts to different agent scaffolds rather than one harness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we perturb the environment a little bit, for example, we change another agent scaffold, then it doesn't generalize

takeaways.what_they_do: They scale environments where coding goals are verifiable so the model can react to real environment feedback and learn from pass/fail rather than static data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can actually target verifiable coding goals and to learn from it
